svg.text: 80 A ESC. 5 A 5 V BEC powers:
80 A ESC. 5 A 5 V BEC powers:
COMMON GROUND (every ground is this one node)
A thin ground wire taps each XT60 and joins the common-ground bus. The MPX connectors carry no ground pin.
2. Layout (each wing self-powered by its own ESC; the fuselage runs on two 5 V buses)
flap 1 L servo, flap 2 L servo
Body bus - ESC-A 5 V via MPX-R:
elevator x2, rudder, bay door x2
Nose bus - ESC-B 5 V via MPX-L:
flap 1 R servo, flap 2 R servo
ESC-A still carries the right wing + most of the fuselage. ESC-B takes its wing + the nose. Watch ESC-A under multi-servo / retract current.
3. Connector pinouts and FC channel map
MPX-R right wing (7/8, no ground pin)
MPX-L left wing (7/8, no ground pin)
RP2350 channel map (LED1 white = no GPIO)
Ground: no MPX pin. All grounds are one common node, joined by a thin tap at each XT60. That common ground also returns the
fuselage power, so keep it solid. Blue label = core flight mixer. Indigo = aux, driven by user-sketch.ino. Red = power.
LED1 (white, always on) taps each wing's local 5 V / GND, no GPIO. LED2 (red left, green right) blinks from one shared GPIO.
